Contribuire ai processi annuali di salary review e di compensazione variabile, sulla base delle valutazioni di performance e delle linee guida stabilite. Ottima padronanza di Microsoft Excel e esperienza con sistemi HRIS (la conoscenza di Zucchetti e SuccessFactors è considerata un plus). Ottima conoscenza della lingua inglese (la conoscenza del francese è considerata un plus). title: COC Master 500GT-3000GT or more than 3000GT (STCW II/2) (Kapitän/in)
description:
The MV Louise Michel is a former French Navy boat we’ve customized to perform search and rescue. Measuring 30 meters in length and capable of up to 28 knots, she was bought with proceeds from the sale of Banksy artwork - who then decorated her with a fire extinguisher. She is operated and crewed by a team of international activist rescue professionals.

- Main responsibilities: handling the ship, overview, control of the vessel and crew safety
- You have the final responsibility for all nautical and technical decisions concerning the operation as well as related crew intructions
- responsible for the ship’s administration (bunkering, crew-lists, customs clearance, detailed operational documentation, daily reports and statistics).
- shiphandling in harbour and during SAR-operations. Together with the officers you will familiarise the crew on the bridge and introduce them to the watch system.
- You will provide the crew with trainings and drills in emergency situations (e.g. what to do in case of fire, POB, ingress of water, unwanted visitors).
- You will work closely with the Head of operations during SAR operations, double checking all decisions against crew and ship safety as well as stability (and guest safety in case of guest already on board).
- You will work closely with the officers and chief engineer

Required:

-EC/EEA-Citizen Passport valid for at least 6 months

-Covid certificate with EU QR code needed, latest vaccine or recovery certificate no older than 180 days or a booster (other nationalities can be transferred to EU certificate)

-Seafarer Medical Certificate (fitness for sea service) according STCW I/9 (Deck Service)

-Proficiency in basic safety (STCW VI/1)

-Proficiency in survival craft and rescue boats other than fast rescue boats (STCW VI/2-1)

-Proficiency in Advanced fire fighting (STCW VI/3)

-Medical First Aid (STCW VI/4-1)

-Medical Care (STCW VI/4-2)

-GMDSS Radio Operator GOC (STCW IV/2)

-COC Master 500GT-3000GT or more than 3000GT (STCW II/2)

-German Endorsement for COC Master Course

-Seafarer's book or the German Seafarer's ID Card

-Excellent and fluent English language skills

-Confidence in decision-making, strong team leading skills, and the ability to cooperate well within a team of volunteers with various levels of nautical experience and skill.

Desired:

- Previous SAR experience
- Italian, French and Arabic language skills

title: Mystery Shopper in Latvia
description:
Mystery Shopper in Latvia

Work tasks: WHAT OUR MYSTERY SHOPPERS DO
Mystery shoppers do not need to be customer service experts, as their personal opinion is not the deciding factor. However, they must be able to assess customer interactions and the service process objectively. We measure how closely employees’ customer service aligns with their company’s service standards and expectations, enabling businesses to identify development needs and provide targeted training. At the same time, we are confident that our mystery shoppers gradually become customer service professionals themselves. We believe this experience increases their value in the job market, especially in customer-facing roles, as we continuously train and guide our mystery shoppers. Our mystery shoppers are welcome to include “Trendline Mystery Shopper” on their CV. For many employers, this demonstrates a solid understanding of customer service processes. WHAT A TRENDLINE MYSTERY SHOPPER DOES NOT DO Trendline mystery shoppers do not provoke or deliberately challenge employees with difficult or misleading questions. Our mystery shoppers visit service providers, banks, retail stores, and sales organizations. The objective is for the mystery shopper to behave like an ordinary customer. This means they do not ask unusual questions that a typical customer would not ask and do not attempt to provoke employees in any way. Mystery shopping visits are conducted according to scenarios provided by Trendline. After each visit, the mystery shopper submits a detailed report through the Trendline online platform.

We offer: https://trendline.lt
Over 25 years of experience in developing customer service and sales organizations. We operate in Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania. Our services include: mystery shopping, training, customer satisfaction surveys and feedback questionnaires, development of customer service standards, production of training videos, and internal audit tools for managers. We provide our clients with a comprehensive solution—from defining customer service standards and principles to employee training and measuring implementation and performance.

Other requirements: WHAT QUALITIES WE LOOK FOR A mystery shopper should be responsible, friendly, honest,
reliable, and willing to follow instructions carefully while maintaining a professional approach. Before applying for assignments, our mystery shoppers can review the available projects, including the scenario, evaluation questionnaire, job description, and compensation. Once an assignment is confirmed, they are free to complete the mystery shopping visit at any convenient time within the specified timeframe. After completing the visit, the mystery shopper submits a concise evaluation report through the mystery shopper module of our online platform. Our mystery shoppers always have access to our dedicated Mystery Shopper Support Service, which provides ongoing assistance to help them complete assignments to a high standard. Upon request, we also offer additional training, as well as technical and practical support. With more than 25 years of experience in training and customer service development, Trendline knows how to focus on what matters most and provides high-quality training for all mystery shoppers.

Option to work from home: Yes

title: Mystery Shopper in Lithuania
description:
Mystery Shopper in Lithuania

Work tasks: WHAT OUR MYSTERY SHOPPERS DO
Mystery shoppers do not need to be customer service experts, as their personal opinion is not the deciding factor. However, they must be able to assess customer interactions and the service process objectively. We measure how closely employees’ customer service aligns with their company’s service standards and expectations, enabling businesses to identify development needs and provide targeted training. At the same time, we are confident that our mystery shoppers gradually become customer service professionals themselves. We believe this experience increases their value in the job market, especially in customer-facing roles, as we continuously train and guide our mystery shoppers. Our mystery shoppers are welcome to include “Trendline Mystery Shopper” on their CV. For many employers, this demonstrates a solid understanding of customer service processes. WHAT A TRENDLINE MYSTERY SHOPPER DOES NOT DO Trendline mystery shoppers do not provoke or deliberately challenge employees with difficult or misleading questions. Our mystery shoppers visit service providers, banks, retail stores, and sales organizations. The objective is for the mystery shopper to behave like an ordinary customer. This means they do not ask unusual questions that a typical customer would not ask and do not attempt to provoke employees in any way. Mystery shopping visits are conducted according to scenarios provided by Trendline. After each visit, the mystery shopper submits a detailed report through the Trendline online platform.

We offer: https://trendline.lt
Over 25 years of experience in developing customer service and sales organizations. We operate in Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania. Our services include: mystery shopping, training, customer satisfaction surveys and feedback questionnaires, development of customer service standards, production of training videos, and internal audit tools for managers. We provide our clients with a comprehensive solution—from defining customer service standards and principles to employee training and measuring implementation and performance.

Other requirements: WHAT QUALITIES WE LOOK FOR
A mystery shopper should be responsible, friendly, honest, reliable, and willing to follow instructions carefully while maintaining a professional approach. Before applying for assignments, our mystery shoppers can review the available projects, including the scenario, evaluation questionnaire, job description, and compensation. Once an assignment is confirmed, they are free to complete the mystery shopping visit at any convenient time within the specified timeframe. After completing the visit, the mystery shopper submits a concise evaluation report through the mystery shopper module of our online platform. Our mystery shoppers always have access to our dedicated Mystery Shopper Support Service, which provides ongoing assistance to help them complete assignments to a high standard. Upon request, we also offer additional training, as well as technical and practical support. With more than 25 years of experience in training and customer service development, Trendline knows how to focus on what matters most and provides high-quality training for all mystery shoppers.

Option to work from home: Yes

title: Mystery Shopper in Lithuania
description:
Mystery Shopper in Lithuania

Work tasks: WHAT OUR MYSTERY SHOPPERS DO
Mystery shoppers do not need to be customer service experts, as their personal opinion is not the deciding factor. However, they must be able to assess customer interactions and the service process objectively. We measure how closely employees’ customer service aligns with their company’s service standards and expectations, enabling businesses to identify development needs and provide targeted training. At the same time, we are confident that our mystery shoppers gradually become customer service professionals themselves. We believe this experience increases their value in the job market, especially in customer-facing roles, as we continuously train and guide our mystery shoppers. Our mystery shoppers are welcome to include “Trendline Mystery Shopper” on their CV. For many employers, this demonstrates a solid understanding of customer service processes. WHAT A TRENDLINE MYSTERY SHOPPER DOES NOT DO Trendline mystery shoppers do not provoke or deliberately challenge employees with difficult or misleading questions. Our mystery shoppers visit service providers, banks, retail stores, and sales organizations. The objective is for the mystery shopper to behave like an ordinary customer. This means they do not ask unusual questions that a typical customer would not ask and do not attempt to provoke employees in any way. Mystery shopping visits are conducted according to scenarios provided by Trendline. After each visit, the mystery shopper submits a detailed report through the Trendline online platform.

We offer: https://trendline.lt
Over 25 years of experience in developing customer service and sales organizations. We operate in Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania. Our services include: mystery shopping, training, customer satisfaction surveys and feedback questionnaires, development of customer service standards, production of training videos, and internal audit tools for managers. We provide our clients with a comprehensive solution—from defining customer service standards and principles to employee training and measuring implementation and performance.

Other requirements: WHAT QUALITIES WE LOOK FOR
A mystery shopper should be responsible, friendly, honest, reliable, and willing to follow instructions carefully while maintaining a professional approach. Before applying for assignments, our mystery shoppers can review the available projects, including the scenario, evaluation questionnaire, job description, and compensation. Once an assignment is confirmed, they are free to complete the mystery shopping visit at any convenient time within the specified timeframe. After completing the visit, the mystery shopper submits a concise evaluation report through the mystery shopper module of our online platform. Our mystery shoppers always have access to our dedicated Mystery Shopper Support Service, which provides ongoing assistance to help them complete assignments to a high standard. Upon request, we also offer additional training, as well as technical and practical support. With more than 25 years of experience in training and customer service development, Trendline knows how to focus on what matters most and provides high-quality training for all mystery shoppers.

Option to work from home: Yes

title: Head of Group Financial Crime Compliance & Group MLRO (m/f)
description:
Head of Group Financial Crime Compliance & Group MLRO

Purpose of the Job

Quintet Private Bank is a leading private bank in the wealth management sector; we are committed to our clients and their families, and pride ourselves on our personalised service based on a deep understanding of what clients want to achieve. We are a bank headquartered in Luxembourg with branches in Belgium, Denmark, Germany, and the Netherlands, as well as a subsidary in the UK. Supervised by the CSSF we have the ambition to stay true to our purpose to be the most trusted fiduciary of family wealth.

When you join us you are joining a company that values diversity of background, equal access to opportunities, career development, collaboration and inclusiveness. We want our employees to feel proud of being part of a company that is committed to do the right thing. You will have the opportunity to grow your career while developing personally and professionally through various resources and programmes.

The Head of Group Financial Crime Compliance & MLRO has primary responsibility for implementation, oversight and monitoring of the Group's financial crime compliance framework (across money laundering & terrorist financing, sanctions, bribery & corruption, external fraud risks), ensuring robust risk management, full regulatory compliance, and effective detection and reporting of financial crime, thereby safeguarding the integrity, reputation, and resilience of the organisation. The role holder acts as the central point of contact with competent authorities and the FIU on financial crime (including specifically AML/CFT ) matters.

Key Accountabilities

Group AML/CFT Framework Leadership:

• Define, implement and maintain a consistent and effective Group-wide FCC framework aligned with applicable regulations and group risk appetite  across all entities.
• Ensure policies, procedures and control expectations are defined, implemented and maintained.    

Group Financial Crime Risk Stewardship:

• Oversee the effectiveness of the financial crime risk control framework .  
• Provide advice,  guidance and challenge to the 1LoD risk and control ownership.  
• Coordinate and maintain the group-wide financial crime risk assessment.

Client Due Diligence Oversight:

• Oversee the effectiveness of client due diligence and client acceptance processes.
• Ensure higher risk clients are subject to enhanced due diligence.
• Monitor compliance with client onboarding and periodic review requirements.            
                        
Suspicious Activity Reporting Oversight:

• Oversee the effectiveness of transaction monitoring and client/transaction screening arrangements including systems/toolings.
• Act as ultimate escalation point for suspicious activity, investigate complex cases and ensure timely and compliant reporting to FIUs.                                    

Regulatory Engagement & Representation:

• Serve as primary contact for regulators, leading inspections, managing regulatory interactions, overseeing regulatory reporting and ensuring remediation of findings for financial crime matters.                                    

Group MLRO Network & Local Oversight:

• Lead and coordinate local MLROs, ensuring consistent governance, escalation, independence and oversight across jurisdictions.
Governance, Board Reporting & Advisory:
• Provide regular FCC reporting to senior management and the Board, advising on risk exposure, control effectiveness and mitigation strategies.
• Ensure escalation of major financial crime risk events, breaches or control issues, ensuring appropriate reporting, documentation and remediation.

Culture, Training & Awareness:

• Promote a strong compliance culture throughout the organisation by designing and delivering effective AML/CFT training and awareness across all levels of the organisation

Knowledge and Experience

• Bachelor's degree in Finance, Law, Business Administration, or a related field.
• Advanced degree or professional certification (e.g., CAMS, CFE) preferred.
• Minimum of 10 years of relevant experience in financial crime compliance within the financial services industry (Larger bank / big four preferred), with a focus on AML, ABC, sanctions, and policy framework.
• In-depth knowledge of European and UK regulatory requirements related to financial crime compliance, including AML directives, sanctions regimes, and bribery/corruption laws.                          
• Proven experience in developing and implementing FCC policies, procedures, and controls across multiple jurisdictions.
• Strong leadership and management skills with the ability to effectively oversee a team and drive results in a dynamic and complex environment.  

Attributes and Qualities

• Leadership & People Management                                
• Collaborative Teamwork                                
• Critical Thinking & Problem Solving                                
• Communication (Verbal & Written)                                
• Conflict Resolution & Negotiation

Technical Skills

• MS Office proficiency

Languages Skills

• English: Fluent
• Any other Quintet language is considered an asset

title: Lower School Learner Support Teacher - 1 year contract (m/f)
description:
Want to help every learner access, participate and thrive?

At the International School of Luxembourg (ISL), we believe that learner diversity enriches our community. We are looking for a Lower School Learner Support Services (LSS) Teacher who is passionate about creating inclusive learning environments where children feel known, valued and empowered to grow.
Working within our learning community, you will support students with language acquisition and/or diverse learning needs, partnering closely with classroom teachers, families and colleagues across Learner Support Services. Through responsive teaching, targeted intervention and inclusive practice, you will help remove barriers to learning and enable students to develop confidence, agency and independence.
Why does this Role matter?
You will be an important advocate for learners and a resource for our whole learning community. Your expertise will help teachers respond to learner variability, help families understand and support their child's development, and—most importantly—help students recognise themselves as capable, active and successful learners. At ISL, learner support is not simply about helping students overcome challenges. It is about creating the conditions in which every child can participate, develop agency, experience success and reach their potential.

Why ISL?
At ISL, you will join a diverse, caring, and forward-thinking community where:
● Learning is driven by curiosity, compassion, and connection
● Educators are supported to grow, reflect, and innovate
● Students are empowered to find their voice and shape their future
At ISL, learning is deeply human. We believe in creating spaces where students feel seen, heard, and inspired to take ownership of their learning. At our school, learning is driven by curiosity, inquiry, and hands-on experimentation. We are looking for teachers who see teaching as relational, creative and purposeful.

What will You do?
● Support learners individually, in small groups and within the classroom through inclusive, evidence-informed language and learning interventions.
● Co-teach and collaborate with classroom teachers to differentiate learning experiences and ensure meaningful access to the IB Primary Years Programme curriculum.
● Build learner agency by involving students in understanding their strengths, setting learning goals and reflecting on their progress.
● Use assessment purposefully to identify learning needs, monitor growth and adapt interventions and support.
● Develop and monitor Individual Learning Plans, accommodations and targeted learning goals for students requiring additional support.
● Case-manage students receiving language or learning support, maintaining clear records and coordinating communication between students, families, teachers and relevant specialists.
● Partner with families, building trusting and respectful relationships around each child's learning, development and wellbeing.
● Collaborate across multidisciplinary teams, including classroom teachers, counsellors, school leaders and external specialists.
● Strengthen inclusive practice by sharing expertise, resources and strategies with teachers and teaching assistants.
● Contribute actively to the wider Learner Support Services Team and our collaborative professional learning culture.
● Taking active part in the vibrant life of the school — from parent evenings to community events to leading beyond-the-classroom activities.
● Engaging in personal professional growth and bring fresh ideas into the classroom.
● Engage with AI effectively in guiding learners by having a human-centered mindset, promoting ethical principles and responsible use, and providing the knowledge, understanding and skills needed to create and use AI to complement their education.
You will thrive here if you …
● Build positive, trusting relationships with children and creates a strong sense of belonging and psychological safety.
● See learner variability through a strengths-based and inclusive lens.
● Differentiate learning thoughtfully and creatively to reduce barriers and increase participation.
● Collaborate effectively and sees co-teaching as a shared professional practice.
● Communicate sensitively and clearly with students, families, colleagues and external specialists.
● Use evidence, observation and assessment to make informed decisions about learning.
● Are organised and dependable when managing individual learning plans, referrals, documentation and confidential information.
● Reflect on your practice, seeks feedback and remains curious about developments in language acquisition and inclusive education.
● Demonstrate cultural responsiveness, empathy and respect within a diverse international community.

Who are You?
● Strong knowledge of inclusive education, learning differences and/or English language acquisition.
● An understanding of multi-tiered systems of support (“MTSS”) and the use of targeted, evidence-informed interventions.
● Experience with co-teaching, differentiation and inclusive classroom practice.
● Able to use assessment information to identify needs, establish goals and monitor student progress.
● Hold a current teaching qualification/certification and a Bachelor's degree or equivalent; a Master's degree in Special/Inclusive Education, Learning Support, Learning Differences or Language Acquisition is highly valued.
● Preferably two years of recent successful experience working with preschool or primary-aged learners with language and/or learning support needs.
● Experience supporting multilingual learners and recognising multilingualism as an asset.
● Experience interpreting psychoeducational assessments and translating recommendations into classroom practice would be an advantage.
● Experience in an international school and/or IB PYP environment is highly valued.
● Near-native fluency in English and confidence using digital tools to support learning, collaboration and documentation.

We are keen to attract applicants from diverse backgrounds, particularly those whose nationality, identity, gender or race is currently under-represented in international education.
We are committed to safeguarding and prioritising the wellbeing of children and young people and expect all staff to share this commitment.
Recruitment timeline:
• If you are shortlisted, you will receive a notification email to book your interview.
• If you have not been contacted after the deadline, your application is potentially unsuccessful but, in any case, you will receive an official answer.

title: AML Governance Officer (m/f)
description:
AML Governance Officer

Location Leudelange
Experience Level Experienced
Home Office Yes, partially possible

Your Job in a Nutshell

The AML Governance Officer is responsible for strengthening and harmonising AML/CFT governance across our EU entities and branches. Working closely with the Group AML/CTF Office in Switzerland and local Compliance teams, you will support the Group-wide AML/CFT Compliance Function, oversee key AML/CFT risks and regulatory developments, and help ensure consistent and effective compliance across Europe.

What you can expect

• Develop, maintain and continuously enhance the EU AML/CFT Governance Framework, ensuring consistent implementation of policies, standards and controls across EU entities.
• Monitor EU and international AML/CFT regulatory developments, assess their impact and coordinate the implementation of new requirements across the organisation.
• Coordinate and provide oversight of the EU-wide ML/TF Risk Assessment, challenging local assessments and ensuring that identified risks are appropriately addressed.
• Act as a key contact for AMLA and other supervisory authorities, coordinating regulatory requests, inspections, submissions and remediation actions.
• Support the EU AML Compliance Manager and Group AML/CTF Office with governance reporting, regulatory analysis, risk monitoring and preparation of management and committee materials.
• Coordinate with local AML Officers and Compliance teams to promote consistent standards, effective information sharing and best practices across jurisdictions.
• Monitor the effectiveness of the AML/CFT governance framework, identify areas for improvement and support audits, regulatory reviews, remediation programmes and training initiatives.
• Build strong relationships with key stakeholders across Compliance, Legal, Risk, Audit and the business to foster a strong AML/CFT governance and compliance culture.

What we expect

• Master's degree in Law, Compliance, Finance, Risk Management or a related field. An AML certification (ACAMS, ICA or equivalent) is an asset.
• 10+ years of experience in AML/CFT, ideally within insurance, banking or financial services, with international exposure.
• Strong knowledge of the EU AML/CFT regulatory framework, including AMLA requirements, EU AML legislation, FATF standards and EBA guidelines.
• Proven experience working with regulators and supervisory authorities.
• Strong analytical, problem-solving, organisational and reporting skills.
• Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with a collaborative and adaptable mindset.
• Very good command of English and French, both written and spoken. Any additional language is an asset.

We are more than a traditional insurance company: we are the personal partner for everyone who wants to feel simply safe. We see the digital age as an opportunity to make our offering even more sustainable, innovative and customer-oriented in the future. Are you shaping it with us?

This role is part of our Information Security Department and will be reporting to an Information Security Manager.

title: Assistant Manager – Fund Accounting (m/f)
description:
Assistant Manager – Fund Accounting

Role Overview

Within the Fund Administration department, the Assistant Manager is responsible for overseeing a portfolio of complex and high‑profile fund structures, ensuring high‑quality service delivery, regulatory compliance, and timely reporting.

The role combines technical expertise, team leadership, and client ownership. The Assistant Manager acts as a key escalation point for both clients and internal teams and supports the Manager in driving operational excellence, risk management, and process improvement.

Tasks

Client & Delivery Ownership

• Act as the primary point of contact for a portfolio of sophisticated clients (Private Equity, Private Debt, Evergreen structures, Hybrid structures, Open-ended structures).
• Assume end‑to‑end responsibility for service delivery, ensuring compliance with SLAs, fund documentation, and regulatory requirements.
• Manage client expectations proactively and handle escalations independently before involving the Manager where required.
Build and maintain trusted, long‑term client relationships, participating in client meetings, onboarding calls, and post‑audit reviews.

Onboarding

During client onboarding, the Assistant Manager undertakes several crucial tasks to ensure a smooth transition and establish a productive relationship with the new client. Hereunder are some key responsibilities:

• Lead or actively support client onboardings, restructurings, migrations, and system set‑ups.
• Validate fund structures, valuation methodologies, fee models, and reporting frameworks in line with legal documents.
• Coordinate across internal teams (FA, TA, back office, Corporate, AIFM, Risk & Compliance, IT etc) to ensure seamless implementation.
• Review and sign‑off data migration and initial NAVs.

NAV Oversight & Technical Review

During Net Asset Value (NAV) oversight, the Assistant Manager play a critical role in ensuring accuracy, compliance, and smooth operations. Hereunder are some key responsibilities:

• Assume overall accountability for the NAV oversight framework across the assigned client portfolio, ensuring accuracy, consistency, timeliness, and compliance with fund documentation, accounting standards, and regulatory requirements.
• Oversee the end‑to‑end NAV production cycle, including capital activity, income recognition, valuation inputs, investor allocations, and fee calculations.
• Perform in‑depth technical reviews and approvals of complex NAVs, including:

o Private equity, private debt, evergreen funds, and multi‑compartment structures
o Complex instruments (loans, profit‑participating notes, derivatives, look‑through investments)
o FX treatments, waterfalls, and performance fee mechanisms
• Act as a technical reference point on Lux GAAP, IFRS, consolidation and structure‑specific treatments.

• Ensure all NAV‑related deliverables meet agreed Service Level Agreements (SLAs) and internal quality standards.
• Maintain strong documentation standards, including working papers, reconciliation files, and management review evidence, to support both internal controls and external audit requirements.
• Support the preparation of financial statements inputs by ensuring consistency between NAVs, accounting records, and statutory reporting.

Risk Management, Controls & Audit

• Act as a key control owner for the assigned client portfolio, ensuring that fund accounting activities are performed in line with internal policies, ISAE requirements, regulatory obligations, and client documentation.
• Ensure that appropriate preventive and detective controls are in place, operating effectively, and evidenced.
• Review and challenge unusual transactions, valuation judgments, late data, or deviations from standard processes.
• Act as the primary escalation point for NAV issues, breaches, or errors, ensuring timely resolution, root‑cause analysis, and clear documentation.
• Act as the primary liaison for external auditors, managing audit queries and timelines.
• Support the Manager in maintaining a strong control culture across the team and client portfolio.

Team Leadership & People Management

• Provide day‑to‑day supervision of Senior Fund Accountants and Fund Accountants within the team.
• Allocate work effectively, taking into account complexity, risk and deadlines.
• Review deliverables prepared by the team and provide structured feedback.
• Support training, development, and performance management of team members.
• Promote a culture of accountability, ownership, collaboration, and quality.
• Escalate capacity, performance, or quality concerns to the Manager with proposed solutions.

Process Improvement & Operational Excellence

• Continuously assess existing fund accounting and reporting processes to identify inefficiencies, risks, and improvement opportunities.
• Actively contribute to system enhancements, automation, and standardisation.
• Support the Manager in implementing new operating models, tools, and best practices.
• Encourage a culture of continuous improvement and risk awareness

Required Experience / Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or Economics
• ACCA (or equivalent) – qualified or advanced stage preferred
• Strong knowledge of Lux GAAP and IFRS (including consolidation)
• 8+ years of experience in fund administration, primarily for closed-ended funds, open-ended funds and evergreen/hybrid funds, with experience in various asset classes (private equity, private debt, listed loans)
• Prior experience reviewing NAVs and supervising team members is essential.
• Experience in capital hedging and portfolio management.
• Added value for candidates familiar with public loans managed through Allvue or WSO platforms.
• Languages: English fluent; French and/or German is an advantage.
• Additional advantage for candidates with experience using Paxus.

Skills/Behavior

In addition to demonstrating IQEQ's Group Values (Authentic, Bold, Collaborative), the Assistant Manager is expected to:

• Take ownership and accountability
• Demonstrate sound judgement and risk awareness
• Lead and develop others
• Communicate clearly with senior stakeholders
• Navigate complexity and ambiguity
• Balance client service with internal control discipline
• Plan, prioritise, and delegate effectively
• Continuously develop technical and leadership skills

title: R&T SCIENTIST IN STRUCTURE – FUNCTION STUDY OF SOLUBLE DIETARY FIBRES (m/f)
employer: Luxembourg Institute of Science and Technology - LIST
description:
Fixed term contract | Belvaux | 24 Months

Are you passionate about research? So are we! Come and join us
The Luxembourg Institute of Science and Technology (LIST) is a leading Research and Technology Organisation (RTO) that drives innovation for the economy and society in Luxembourg and beyond. With cutting-edge expertise in Natural, Built, Industrial environments, Space, AI, Security and defence technologies. LIST bridges scientific excellence and applied research to design solutions that address real-world challenges and create positive impact.
Do you want to know more about LIST? Check our website: https://www.list.lu/

How will you contribute?
As part of the Biotechnology Unit, and particularly the Bioformulation Group, you will contribute to the machine learning assisted structure-function study of soluble dietary fibres (galactomannans) isolated from underexplored leguminous seed bioresources in the framework of the ENTANGLE FNR funded project. You will develop clean label procedures to extract and isolate galactomannans from forage legume seed biomass such as alfalfa and clover. In addition, the successful candidate is expected to determine the technofunctional and prebiotic potential of native and enzymatically modified derivatives benchmarked to commercial biopolymer targets.

As a Postdoctoral Researcher, you will mainly be responsible for:
• Extracting, isolating and purifying galactomannans from forage legume seeds
• Enzymatically tailor the chemical structure and technofunctional profile of native galactomannans
• Determine the structure conformational, technological and prebiotic potential of the native and modified galactomannans and
• Promoting and disseminating your research work through high-quality scientific publications in peer-reviewed journals, oral and poster presentations in conferences, and patents.
If you are specialised in food biopolymers, colloids science, and/or food process engineering, with a strong foundation in soft-matter physics and a focus on understanding and tailoring structure–property–function relationships for innovative food applications, please apply and join our new and dynamic team.

About us
The University of Luxembourg is an international research university with a distinctly multilingual and interdisciplinary character.
The Faculty of Law, Economics and Finance counts over 2,700 students enrolled across four Bachelor programmes, thirteen Master programmes, doctoral studies as well as several continuing education courses. The Faculty hosts the Doctoral School of Law and the Doctoral School in Economics, Finance and Management.
Teaching and research at the FDEF benefit from the proximity of European institutions, Luxembourg's leading international financial centre, as well as its vibrant business community. Institutional and private sector partnerships, sponsored chairs and a growing network of international partner universities make the FDEF a dynamic academic hub at the heart of Europe.

Your role
The successful candidate will strengthen the Department of Law's research area in Banking, Financial and Commercial Law, which is a cornerstone of the Department's academic profile and a key contributor to the University's reputation. They will pursue research and teaching in this field, focussing on Luxembourg, EU, and comparative transnational perspectives. The position is of particular strategic relevance given the Department's ambition to maintain its leadership in financial law, a domain central to Luxembourg's role as a global financial centre.
The ideal candidate shows potential to:
• Develop an internationally recognized research profile in banking law in a broad sense, e.g., prudential regulation and bank supervision, depositary law, regulation of payments and payment systems, financial technologies, sustainable finance, secured transactions and consumer financial contracts, links to financial markets law
• Publish extensively in top-tier peer-reviewed journals, monographs, or authoritative treatises
• Contribute to interdisciplinary initiatives such as the FutureFinTechNCER and/or collaborate with the Department of Finance in the field of sustainable finance
• Teach in core areas of banking law. The ability to contribute to teaching in related areas of commercial law—such as financial and securities law, company law, insolvency law, the law of commercial contracts and torts - is an asset
• Cover legal frameworks at both EU and Luxembourg levels, adopting a comparative approach that includes neighbouring jurisdictions and other global financial centres
• Engage with Luxembourg and EU regulators (e.g. CSSF, CBL, ECB, ESMA), international organizations, e.g. IOSCO, BIS, FSB, etc., and other stakeholders, e.g. (inter )national law firms, industry and academic associations
• Acquire competitive research funding and establish and lead their own research team
• Show and develop leadership potential
The candidate will join one of Europe's most prominent academic groups in banking and financial law, distinguished by both its intellectual strength and research output. They will actively contribute to the University's “Third Mission” by engaging with Luxembourg and EU financial law, and will be encouraged to develop into a leadership role within the Department. This position offers the opportunity to gain recognition and respect in Luxembourg's legal community, renowned for its emphasis on financial law expertise and its strong integration of academic insight with professional practice. Their doctoral students will benefit from a strong academic environment and excellent career prospects—more than 20 former PhD graduates from the Department have gone on to become professors.

Your profile
• A Bachelor's, Master's, and PhD degree in Law
• Experience and interest in engaging in academic research at the highest level

• Potential and aptitude for teaching and supervising research at the university level
• An excellent academic track record demonstrating both scholarly excellence and leadership potential
• Experience with externally funded research projects and interdisciplinarity is considered to be an asset
• Experience in interdisciplinary research—particularly at the intersection of law, finance, and technology—is a strong asset

The successful candidate is also expected to collaborate with internal and external stakeholders, prepare grant applications for external funding and actively engage with other research institutions and industry partners to establish research cooperations in Luxembourg and beyond.

title: PhD CANDIDATE IN SOCIAL CRITERIA DRIVEN ABSOLUTE ENVIRONMENTAL.... (m/f)
employer: Luxembourg Institute of Science and Technology - LIST
description:
Fixed term contract | Belvaux | 48 months

Are you passionate about research? So are we! Come and join us

The Luxembourg Institute of Science and Technology (LIST) is a leading Research and Technology Organisation (RTO) that drives innovation for the economy and society in Luxembourg and beyond. With cutting-edge expertise in Natural, Built, Industrial environments, Space, AI, Security and defence technologies. LIST bridges scientific excellence and applied research to design solutions that address real-world challenges and create positive impact.

The Environmental Sustainability Assessment and Circularity (SUSTAIN) Unit conducts cross disciplinary research to support the transition toward a more sustainable, resilient, and healthy society. SUSTAIN combines expertise in environmental sciences, circular economy, risk and safety assessment, and sustainable innovation to address complex challenges related to human and environmental health, climate change, and resource efficiency, developing knowledge, methods, and transferable software for the simulation and comprehensive sustainability assessment of socio-economic systems. Its purpose is to foster sustainable eco-innovation, through products and technologies, as well as support sustainability-oriented policy implementation and behavioural change to promote decarbonisation transitions.

Do you want to know more about LIST? Check our website: https://www.list.lu/

How will you contribute?

The world faces a convergence of crises that are transforming the conditions for human development. Climate instability, ecosystem degradation, and the overuse of natural resources have reached critical levels, while social inequality, political fragmentation, and technological disruption are reshaping societies. Traditional notions of economic competitiveness, centred on growth and productivity, are being redefined to include social resilience, inclusiveness, and ecological integrity. Responding to this “polycrisis” requires new pathways that reconcile prosperity with planetary and social limits. Luxembourg offers a particularly illustrative example of these tensions. The country enjoys one of the highest income levels globally and a dynamic financial and business environment that sustains its reputation for economic success. Yet this prosperity depends strongly on cross-border commuting, which creates mobility challenges and environmental stress. Escalating housing prices have made access to affordable living increasingly difficult, displacing a significant share of the workforce beyond national borders. The reliance on imported energy leaves households and firms vulnerable to external shocks. Although Luxembourg's welfare model and social dialogue remain robust, they are under pressure from rising costs of living, widening inequalities, and growing demands on public services. Environmentally, Luxembourg's footprint per inhabitant ranks among the largest worldwide, driven by high consumption and land-use pressures that push the country beyond sustainable limits.

Meeting these intertwined challenges calls for coordinated transformations that bridge sectors, disciplines, and scales. Economic and social progress must be reframed within the concept of a Safe Operating Space—an area in which human well-being is achieved without breaching environmental boundaries. The objective is to steer innovation, governance, and everyday practices toward forms of competitiveness that are compatible with sustainability, rather than in conflict with it. The Doctoral Training Unit C-SOS (Competitiveness within a Safe Operating Space) is designed to cultivate researchers capable of analysing and fostering such transformations. It brings together an interdisciplinary consortium to train 12 PhD candidates in the assessment and design of inclusive and sustainable development trajectories. The programme equips them with conceptual and methodological tools to connect environmental sustainability, social well-being, and economic dynamics into integrated frameworks for decision-making. Its ambition is to inform socio-economic policies, encourage responsible industrial and technological innovation, and contribute to more equitable and resilient societies. Luxembourg provides an ideal environment for this initiative, combining strong expertise in sustainability science and policy analysis. The DTU is a collaboration between researchers at the Luxembourg Institute of Science and Technology (LIST), the University of Luxembourg (UL) and the Urban Development and Mobility Department at the Luxembourg Institute of Socio-Economic Research (LISER). The consortium also includes the National Statistics Office (STATEC). In this DTU, 12 scientists will train 12 PhD students over six years (from January 2027), each obtaining a PhD from UL's doctoral schools.

As part of the C-SOS Doctoral Training Unit, in this PhD you will integrate concepts from Post-Growth, Sufficiency and Doughnut Economics into the downscaling of planetary boundaries, leveraging good examples of application to territories and cities. Possible research questions include: how to couple ecological limits and social foundation as an interdependent system? How to define social foundation? How to allocate the carrying capacity based on social foundation?.

You will be embedded in the SUSTAIN unit at LIST and enrolled as a doctoral candidate at the University of Luxembourg. title: RESEARCHER IN FIRST-PRINCIPLES MODELLING OF MULTIFERROIC MATERIALS (m/f)
employer: Luxembourg Institute of Science and Technology - LIST
description:
Fixed term contract | Belvaux | 24 months

Are you passionate about research? So are we! Come and join us

The Luxembourg Institute of Science and Technology (LIST) is a leading Research and Technology Organisation (RTO) that drives innovation for the economy and society in Luxembourg and beyond. With cutting-edge expertise in Natural, Built, Industrial environments, Space, AI, Security and defence technologies. LIST bridges scientific excellence and applied research to design solutions that address real-world challenges and create positive impact.

Do you want to know more about LIST? Check our website: https://www.list.lu/

How will you contribute?

The push to reduce global energy consumption has set a clear trend in modern technology towards devices that are smaller, faster and more energy-efficient. Meeting these demands calls for new materials that can perform several functions at once. Magnetoelectric multiferroics are especially attractive in this respect, because they combine magnetism and ferroelectricity in a single phase. Crucially, this opens the possibility of controlling magnetism with an electric field which could enable entirely new device architectures and transform modern computing and data storage. Despite decades of progress, this promise is hard to realise: in most known multiferroics the two orders only coexist well below room temperature, and many are difficult to integrate with standard semiconductor manufacturing. Turning multiferroics into a practical technology therefore requires identifying or designing new materials that show robust, coupled magnetism and ferroelectricity at room temperature and remain compatible with established fabrication processes.

This is the challenge at the heart of the SMART project funded by the FNR CORE programme and led by Natalya Fedorova. We offer a 2-year postdoc position in which you will use first-principles calculations (DFT) together with analytical modelling to design room-temperature multiferroics via doping of semiconductors. Working mainly with DFT, you will carry out a systematic analysis of electronic, structural, magnetic and ferroelectric properties of these materials - computing, for instance, ground-state magnetic configurations, magnetic exchange interactions, electric polarization and polarization-switching pathways. You will then combine these results with analytical models to describe the magnetoelectric coupling in the most promising candidates and to explore how their magnetism could be manipulated with an applied electric field.

You will join the Modelling of Functional Materials group led by Jorge Íñiguez-González (also involved in the project) and will benefit from interactions with other team members.

How will you contribute?
You'll be working on a production-grade Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) system purpose-built for second-level controls on NAV computation in investment funds. The system must retrieve relevant regulatory methodology, replicate calculation steps, detect discrepancies against fund accounting outputs, and produce control reports that are traceable, auditable, and defensible under regulatory scrutiny.
You will contribute to a system where precision, explainability, and reliability are non-negotiable.

Code Development (60%):
·          Build retrieval pipelines optimised for structured regulatory methodology documents (CSSF circulars, ESMA guidelines, fund prospectuses), with adaptive weighting to surface the specific calculation rules relevant to each control query
·          Implement numerical validation pipelines that compare LLM-derived NAV calculation outputs against fund administrator figures, applying configurable tolerance bands and discrepancy flagging logic
·          Implement chunking strategies optimised for fund accounting reports and regulatory circulars, preserving the structure of calculation tables, formula references, and numbered regulatory provisions.
·          Build evaluation frameworks measuring control accuracy (error detection rate, false positive/negative rates on flagged discrepancies) and the quality of generated audit reports
·          Optimise vector database indexing for regulatory document corpora with high update frequency, ensuring fast retrieval as new CSSF/ESMA guidance is published

Research & experimentation (25%):
·          Benchmark embedding models against the current Nomic Embed Text baseline, with a focus on sensitivity to numerical and regulatory language in fund accounting contexts
·          Explore cross-lingual retrieval for EU regulatory documents published across multiple languages, with emphasis on French and German variants of CSSF and ESMA guidance
·          Research agent-based simulation of NAV calculation steps, investigating how LLMs can reason reliably over arithmetic-sensitive regulatory workflows and signal confidence levels
·          Experiment with multi-agent orchestration for second-level control workflows, where agents decompose a NAV control task into parallel verification sub-tasks across pricing, accruals, and corporate actions.

System integration (15%):
·          Integrate LLM backends optimised for structured reasoning and develop prompt engineering patterns that enforce step-by-step calculation verification and explainable output
·          Implement comprehensive logging, structured audit trail generation, and monitoring dashboards that allow compliance officers to review and challenge control decisions

description:
Permanent contract | Belval

Are you passionate about space resources? So are we! Come and join us

The European Space Resources Innovation Centre (ESRIC) is a joint initiative of the Luxembourg Space Agency (LSA), the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Luxembourg Institute of Science and Technology (LIST). ESRIC's mission is to be an internationally recognized centre of expertise for scientific, technical, business and economic aspects related to the use of space resources for human and robotic exploration, as well as for a future in-space economy.

The primary objective of ESRIC is to research, develop and improve our knowledge and understanding of space resources, and the performance of processes enabling the utilization of space resources with an initial focus on the Moon.
The Luxembourg Institute of Science and Technology (LIST) is a leading Research and Technology Organisation (RTO) that drives innovation for the economy and society in Luxembourg and beyond. With cutting-edge expertise in Natural, Built, Industrial environments, Space, AI, Security and defence technologies. LIST bridges scientific excellence and applied research to design solutions that address real-world challenges and create positive impact.

Do you want to know more about ESRIC and LIST? Check our websites: https://www.esric.lu/ and https://www.list.lu/

How will you contribute?

As part of a new phase of growth for ESRIC, we are seeking a Head of Group for the Space Resources Innovation Ecosystem group. This group promotes innovation within and outside of ESRIC through a unique combination of programmes, infrastructure and initiatives, including programmes to support early-stage ventures in space resources and the operation of infrastructure such as Europe's largest Dusty Thermal Vacuum Chamber. The group works closely with ESRIC's strategic partner ESA across many of its activities. We are looking for a Head of Group with proven experience of leading space resources innovation initiatives, and who understand the specific needs of this emerging sector and the central role that ESRIC can occupy.

Reporting to the Head of ESRIC, the Head of the Space Resources Innovation Ecosystem will be engaged in the definition, execution and implementation of projects and programmes that lead innovation in space resources, both commercial and technical (e.g. increasing TRL).    In coordination with the Head of ESRIC, you will define the group's roadmap and its objectives, and manage the current and future project portfolio. title: Program Manager, Instore Experience (ISX), Reverse Logistic Services (RLS) (m/f)
description:
Program Manager, Instore Experience (ISX), Reverse Logistic Services (RLS)
Job ID: 10541583 | Amazon EU Sarl

Description

Reverse Logistics Services (RLS) exists to make returns effortless and reliable for every Amazon customer — no matter which store or partner they walk into. In France, we deliver that experience across more than 15,000 partner and carrier locations, through convenience-led options such as Label-Free, Box-Free (LFBF) drop-off and every other way a customer can return an item in-store.

The ISX Regional Program Manager, France owns the quality and consistency of that experience across the whole French network. Because returns run through thousands of independent partner sites, the experience can vary widely from one location to the next and the core of this role is closing that gap. You will get into the field, see how returns actually happen at partner locations, coach partners and their teams to the standard customers expect, and use data to focus your time on the sites that need help most. Your mission is holistic: improving in-store returns execution across all return types, so a customer's experience is just as good at the busiest location as it is at the smallest.

This is not only a field-execution role. It carries a strategic remit that reflects its level. Beyond coaching individual sites, you will help design and deploy the network-wide improvements that lift the entire France network at once: in-store signage and wayfinding, store supplies and replenishment mechanisms, associate support and training, and the tools partners rely on to process returns. You will translate what you learn in the field into scalable programs, work across internal teams to launch them in France, and help shape how the broader EU standards themselves are built, turning local, on-the-ground insight into lasting structural improvement.

This is also a founding, build-from-scratch role. You'll be the first ISX Program Manager for France and one of the earliest members of the EU field team, reporting directly to the EU ISX Senior Manager. There's no established playbook yet, you'll help create it. We're looking for someone with real ambition, comfort with ambiguity, and the judgment to focus relentlessly on the initiatives that matter most while the team, tools, and standards are still taking shape.

Key job responsibilities

• Own the in-store returns experience in France across ~17,000 partner and carrier locations, ensuring returns are fast, easy, and reliable for customers across all return types.
• Get into the field and coach. Visit partner locations, observe how returns are handled, and coach partner teams to Amazon's standards for speed, accuracy, and customer experience.
• Use data to prioritize. You can't be everywhere. Use performance data to identify the locations and partners falling furthest behind and concentrate your effort where it improves the customer experience most.
• Drive measurable improvement on the metrics that define a great returns experience: how fast customers are served, how reliably returns are processed, customer satisfaction, and site readiness.
• Deploy network-wide improvements. Lead the rollout of scalable programs that raise the standard across the entire Italian network, including in-store signage and wayfinding, store supplies and replenishment, associate support and training, and returns-processing tools , using your field insight to prioritize and adapt them for the market.
• Shape strategy from the field. Turn on-the-ground observations into recommendations that influence how EU-wide returns standards, mechanisms, and programs are designed, ensuring the field perspective is built in from the start.
• Manage performance to resolution. Follow a structured coaching and follow-up cycle for underperforming sites, and partner with the right internal teams (Business Partnerships for retail partners, the Transportation team for carriers) when issues need to be escalated to a partner's leadership.
• Build the foundation. As a founding team member, help shape how the EU field team audits, coaches, and reports, adapting proven practices from the North America team to the French market and feed your field insights into the monthly ISX reporting that informs strategy.

A day in the life

You start the week by reviewing performance data for France and identifying the partner locations and carriers falling furthest behind on the customer experience. You spend time in the field visiting a risk-weighted set of those sites, watching real customers complete returns, checking that the process is running smoothly, and coaching partner teams on the spot. Back at your desk, you're also driving the French rollout of a new signage standard and a store-supplies replenishment mechanism, using what you saw in the field to shape how they're deployed. You log your findings, build improvement plans for the sites that need them, escalate the bigger systemic issues to the right internal team, and close the week by capturing insights for the monthly ISX report and re-planning around wherever the customer experience needs you most.

About the team

Reverse Logistics Services (RLS) owns the returns journey end-to-end for Amazon, everything that happens after a customer decides to send something back until delivery at our FC. Our purpose is simple but hard: make returns effortless and reliable for every customer, while running one of the largest, most complex reverse-logistics networks in retail.

Within RLS, the In-Store Experience (ISX) team focuses on where returns meet the real world, the thousands of partner and carrier locations customers walk into to drop off an item. We turn a single promise into a consistent reality across every one of them: fast, easy, dependable returns, no matter which door a customer chooses. Working from the field, we close the gap between the best and worst locations, coach partners to a standard customers can count on, and build the mechanisms that lift the whole network at once.

Our culture is hands-on, data-driven, and high-ownership. We obsess over the customer, thrive in ambiguity, dive deep into the details on the ground, and think big about how to scale what works - because the best decisions about in-store returns are made by people who've seen them happen firsthand.

employer: Commerz Real AG Commerz Real Düsseldorf
description:
Willkommen im Team als

(Senior) Risk Manager

Das Unternehmen:

Die Commerz Real Fundmanagement S.à r.l. (“CRFM“) ist ein Spezialist für die Verwaltung von Alternativen Investmentfonds. Die CRFM trägt hierdurch zum Profil der Commerz Real AG und ihren Konzerngesellschaften (“Commerz Real Gruppe“) als integrierter Investmentdienstleister bei. Die CRFM arrangiert Alternative Investmentfonds, insbesondere für Immobilien, Infrastrukturprojekte, Anlagen zur Erzeugung erneuerbarer Energien sowie Großmobilien (wie z.B.: Flugzeuge, Schiffe und Schienenfahrzeuge). Die CRFM ist eine Tochtergesellschaft der Commerz Real AG, die ihrerseits eine Tochter der Commerzbank Aktiengesellschaft, Deutschland, ist.

Aufgabe:

- Als (Senior) Risk Manager Anlageprodukte und Teil des Risk Management Teams bist Du verantwortlich für die Risikoanalyse, Bewertung und Überwachung von (komplexen) Neu- und Bestandsgeschäften unter Beachtung von wirtschaftlichen, rechtlichen und steuerlichen Rahmenbedingungen hinsichtlich aller relevanten Risikoarten (u.a. Adressausfall-, Objektwertänderungs-, Marktpreis-, Liquiditätsrisiken, spezielle Risiken im Bereich Infrastructure wie z.B. Betriebs- und Projektentwicklungsrisiken, etc.)
- Dabei stellst Du die kompetenzgerechte Genehmigung bzw. Erstellung von Genehmigungsvorlagen für An- und Verkaufstransaktionen der AIF/Spezial-AIF sicher
- Zu Deinen Aufgaben gehört auch die Mitarbeit bei der Strukturierung und Steuerung von AIF/Spezial-AIF zur haftungsmäßigen und wirtschaftlichen Optimierung
- Ebenso verantwortest Du die regelmäßige risikotechnische Überwachung der AIF/Spezial-AIF im Wertschöpfungsprozess inkl. Überwachung der vertraglichen Finanzierungsgestaltung und des Liquiditätsmanagements
- Du unterstützt die Marktbereiche bei Vertragsverhandlungen im Neu- und Bestandsgeschäft sowie bei der Entwicklung von neuen Produkten als Mitglied in Dealteams und/oder Projektgruppen
- Die Leitung von bzw. Mitarbeit in bereichsinternen Projekten zur Optimierung / Digitalisierung der Risikoorganisation, hier insbesondere zur (Weiter-)Entwicklung von gesetzeskonformen Prozessen, Regularien und Risikotools gehört ebenfalls zu Deinen Aufgaben
- Du bringst Deine Expertise und Unterstützung bei übergreifenden Projekten sowie im Rahmen der Digitalisierungsstrategie ein. Dabei übernimmst Du auch die Leitung von übergreifenden Projekten
- Du übernimmst Coaching / Weiterbildungsaufgaben im Risikomanagement sowie die Ausbildung von Nachwuchskräften

Profil:

- Erfolgreich abgeschlossenes (auch berufsintegriertes) Studium mit der Fachrichtung Wirtschaftswissenschaften oder Rechtswissenschaften, idealerweise im Schwerpunkt Risikomanagement
- Langjährige fachbezogene Berufserfahrung im Bereich Risikomanagement eines Asset-Managers, eines Fondsemissionshauses oder eines Kreditinstitutes,
- Umfassende Kenntnisse und mehrjährige Erfahrung in der Assetklasse Infrastructure, idealerweise auch in Private Equity und Debt Strukturen. Grundkenntnisse und Interesse an den Assetklassen Renewable Energies, sowie Real Estate runden Deine Erfahrung ab.
- Erweiterte betriebswirtschaftliche Kenntnisse insbesondere im Bereich Risikomanagement, Bilanzanalyse, Discounted Cash-Flow-Analyse, Sensitivitätsanalyse, Cash-Flow-Modellierung, Liquiditätsrisikomanagement und Portfoliosteuerung
- Sehr gute Kenntnisse der einschlägigen Gesetze, Verordnungen, Vorschriften und Richtlinien (AIFM-Richtlinie, AIFM-VO, ESMA-Leitlinien, Luxemburger Gesetze bzgl. AIFMD, u.a.)
- Ausgeprägte analytische Fähigkeiten und sehr sicherer Umgang mit MS Office
- Gute Englischkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift, idealerweise auch gute Französischkenntnisse
- Ausgeprägte Team- und Kommunikationsfähigkeit
- Hohes Maß an Zielstrebigkeit und Eigeninitiative sowie unternehmerisches Denken und Flexibilität

title: Infirmier diplômé (m/f/d)
description:
Infirmier diplômé (m/f/d)


Chez quelqu'un à domicile, vous n'êtes pas simplement là pour réaliser un soin. Vous êtes souvent la présence soignante la plus régulière dans leur vie. Un patient qui vous ouvre sa porte vous fait confiance avant même de vous connaître — et chez Verbandskëscht, nous cherchons des infirmier(ère)s qui prennent cette responsabilité au sérieux, et qui y trouvent du sens.

Sur le terrain :

• Prendre en charge une tournée de patients à domicile au sein d'une équipe pluridisciplinaire, en lien étroit avec votre cadre de soins.
• Réaliser l'ensemble des soins infirmiers prescrits, avec une expertise particulière en soins de plaies.
• Observer, analyser et adapter votre approche : chaque patient est différent, chaque situation évolue.
• Assurer la continuité du lien entre le patient, sa famille et le reste de l'équipe.

Au sein de l'équipe :

• Participer activement aux transmissions et aux réunions pluridisciplinaires.
• Contribuer à la qualité globale des soins en partageant vos observations et votre expertise.
• Évoluer dans une organisation certifiée Great Place to Work, où la qualité des soins est une conviction partagée — pas un argument de communication.

CE QUE NOUS RECHERCHONS

Prérequis :

• Autorisation d'exercer la profession d'infirmier(ère) au Luxembourg.
• Maîtrise du luxembourgeois et du français, indispensable pour créer un lien de confiance avec vos patients.
• Permis B valide.

Qualités recherchées :

• Sens clinique aiguisé — vous repérez ce qui change, ce qui inquiète, ce qui n'est pas dit.
• Rigueur et autonomie dans l'organisation de votre tournée, sans perdre le sens du collectif.
• Capacité à établir une relation de confiance, même lors de visites courtes.
• Une expérience en milieu hospitalier ou extrahospitalier est appréciée.

CE QUE VOUS TROUVEREZ CHEZ NOUS

• Une organisation certifiée Great Place to Work — parce qu'un collaborateur bien entouré prend de meilleurs soins.
• Des formations continues pour rester à la pointe, accessibles à tous les collaborateurs.
• Une culture où l'exigence professionnelle et la bienveillance ne s'opposent pas — elles se renforcent.
• Des conditions de travail à la hauteur de votre engagement, selon le Contrat collectif SAS en vigueur.
• Une équipe pluridisciplinaire qui travaille vraiment ensemble — coordinateurs, infirmiers, aides-soignants, thérapeutes.

Les candidatures sont traitées en toute confidentialité.

The University of Luxembourg is an international research university with a distinctly multilingual and interdisciplinary character.

Through its dual mission of teaching and research, the FSTM seeks to generate and disseminate knowledge and train new generations of responsible citizens in order to better understand, explain and advance society and the environment we live in.
The Department of Engineering (DoE) is a dynamic, interdisciplinary group engaged in civil, electrical, mechanical engineering and operations research/management, driving forward innovative research and solutions. It also has an internationally leading profile in computational science and engineering. We develop cutting-edge technologies, promoting the sustainable and economical use of resources, and meeting the technological demands of Luxembourg, the Greater Region, and beyond. Nearly all research projects are supported by a network of national and international partnerships, several with public or industrial stakeholders. At the University, the Department cooperates across faculties and with the interdisciplinary centres. In particular, the new interdisciplinary centre focused on complex environmental systems opens up significant opportunities for future collaborations.

The candidate will work closely with the TSU Team Leader and technicians to support the DoE members (PhD students, Post-doctoral researchers, professors), in their research activities, specially in the fields of Concrete, Steel, Composite and Geotechnical structures. • Ability in executing standard workshop jobs. e.g., concrete casting
• Adaptability and willingness to learn new skills
• Ability to work proactively, independently
• Team spirit, dynamism and sense of initiative
• Flexibility
• Good command of MS Office tools: Outlook, Word, Excel
• Excellent command (C1) of English is required. Good working knowledge (B1) of French, German and Luxembourgish would be an advantage

• A modern, dynamic university with a personal and inclusive atmosphere. Multilingual and international character. Staff coming from more than 90 countries. Member of The Guild of European Research Intensive Universities

Pwc Luxembourg is hiring a Manager Customs & Trade Facilitation, Government and Public Sector Advisory (m/f/d). What if it was you?

Our clients are customs administrations, customs unions, ministries, and international institutions (EU, GCC, WBG, UN and beyond) seeking to transform, modernise, and align with international trade facilitation standards. This is a full-time, on-site position based in Luxembourg, with frequent international travel.

Be a part of our team where you will:  

• Lead and deliver consulting engagements for customs and tax administrations, customs unions, and international institutions, covering transformation, modernisation, and trade facilitation reform agendas;
• Take ownership of projects in the domain of Single Window, interoperability, and data exchange workstreams, advising clients on architecture, governance, applicable international standards (e.g. WCO Data Model, UN/CEFACT), and implementation roadmaps;

• Coach junior consultants and trainees, structure complex multi-workstream engagements, and ensure the quality and consistency of deliverables (reports, frameworks, presentations).

Let's talk about you. If you …
  
• Have at least 10 years of relevant experience in trade facilitation, customs modernisation, or Single Window implementation, including assignments delivered for or with public administrations and international organisations (e.g. UN, WCO, WTO, EU, WBG, regional development banks);
• Bring hands-on expertise in areas such as Single Window design and implementation, customs IT systems architecture, customs-to-customs data exchange, or cross-border digital trade, with a solid understanding of international standards (WCO, UN/CEFACT, WTO TFA);

title: Group General Counsel - International Company (m/f)
description:
JOB DESCRIPTION

Group General Counsel

Reporting line: Chief Executive Officer, with dotted reporting line to the Board.
Contract: permanent, full-time (40 hours per week). Location: Luxembourg, hybrid, with regular international travel.

1 The business and the role

The company operates an international online subscription and creator platform, with exposure to adult content, and which operates across the United Kingdom, the European Union and the US. The Group General Counsel is the most senior legal officer of the group.

2 Main responsibilities

1. Legal function leadership and Board support

• Build, staff and lead the group legal function, including recruitment, budget, external counsel panel and legal operations.
• Act as principal legal adviser to the Board, the founders and the executive team, and attend Board and committee meetings.
• Set and own the group's legal risk appetite, escalation framework and legal reporting to the Board and to investors.
• Manage disputes and litigation across jurisdictions, including instruction and supervision of external counsel.

2. Corporate, M&A and governance

• Lead corporate and M&A transactions end to end, including target assessment, due diligence, transaction documentation, signing, closing and PMI.
• Support fundraising rounds, investor documentation, shareholder arrangements and cap table matters.
• Own corporate governance across a multi-jurisdictional holding structure, including entity management, board and shareholder resolutions, statutory filings, registers of beneficial owners, delegated authority frameworks and group policies.
• Act as secretary to the Board and to group entity boards, or supervise that function.
• Coordinate with finance and tax on group structuring, intragroup agreements, transfer pricing documentation and substance requirements.

3. Data protection, artificial intelligence and digital regulation

• Own the group's data protection compliance programme under the EU GDPR and the UK GDPR, including records of processing, transfer mechanisms, data protection impact assessments, data subject rights, breach response and supervisory authority engagement.
• Advise on US privacy legislation applicable to the group's user base, including state level comprehensive privacy laws and applicable wiretapping and tracking technology claims.
• Own the group's artificial intelligence governance framework, including the classification of AI systems, transparency obligations for synthetic and AI generated content, model and vendor due diligence, training data and intellectual property questions, and readiness for the EU AI Act.
• Advise on the EU Digital Services Act and the UK Online Safety Act, including notice and action mechanisms, trusted flaggers, transparency reporting, risk assessment obligations, illegal content duties and children's access assessments.
• Advise on the EU Digital Markets Act, the audiovisual media services framework and platform to business regulation as applicable to the group's distribution channels.

4. High risk industry, trust and safety, and content compliance

• Advise on the legal and regulatory framework applicable to adult oriented and creator monetization platforms, including age assurance and identity verification, performer consent and record keeping obligations, nonconsensual intimate image takedown, CSAM prevention and reporting, and content moderation and appeals.
• Design and maintain creator terms, model releases, content licences, revenue share arrangements and agency and management arrangements.
• Advise on advertising, affiliate and performance marketing arrangements, influencer marketing rules and consumer protection requirements in the EU, the UK and the US.
• Manage intellectual property, including trademarks, copyright enforcement and anti-piracy programmes.

5. Payments, financial crime and sanctions

• Own the legal side of the group's payments stack, including acquirer and payment service provider agreements, alternative payment methods, payout and creator disbursement arrangements and merchant of record structures.
• Advise on card scheme rules as they apply to high risk and adult merchant categories, including high brand risk and integrity risk registration programmes, prohibited content rules, chargeback thresholds and remediation plans.
• Advise on PSD2 and strong customer authentication, electronic money and payment institution perimeter questions, and the implications of the EU instant payments and payment services reform.
• Own the group's KYC, AML, CTF and sanctions framework, including creator onboarding, transaction monitoring, and screening against EU, UK, US OFAC and other relevant measures.

6. Commercial and employment

• Negotiate the group's material commercial agreements, including technology, content, distribution, partnership and vendor agreements.
• Support the people function on employment law across multiple jurisdictions, including contracts, contractor classification, incentive schemes and internal investigations.

3 Required profile

The following are requirements (must-haves):

• Law degree from an EU or EEA or UK university.
• Admission in good standing to the bar of an EU or EEA Member State or UK.
• A minimum of 20 years of PQE legal experience, of which at least 10 years in a senior in house legal leadership role (General Counsel, Head of Legal or equivalent).
• Demonstrable experience of building and leading an international in house legal team across diverse jurisdictions.
• A track record of leading cross border M&A transactions in the US, UK and/or EU jurisdictions.
• Corporate governance experience in complex international structures.
• Recognised privacy certification (IAPP CIPP/E or equivalent) and hands on ownership of a GDPR compliance programme.
• Direct working knowledge of the EU/UK digital regulatory framework, including DSA, DMA, OSA, the AI Act, AVMS.
• Substantive experience in high risk regulated industries, and specifically in adult entertainment or creator platform compliance.
• Substantive experience of payment processing and billing for high-risk merchant categories.
• Experience in entertainment and media.
• Tax, KYC/AML and sanctions experience in a regulated or high risk environment.
• Experience advising founders, C level executives and Boards in a venture backed, high growth environment.
• English at level C (native/bilingual/proficient user).

The following are advantages (nice to haves):

• Postgraduate business qualification (MBA or equivalent).
• Formal training or certification in AI
• Recognised corporate governance certification (e.g. ILA CGO).
• Qualification or formal training in international taxation and in corporate compliance.
• Experience of a Luxembourg holding structure and of Luxembourg corporate and employment law.
• Additional languages, in particular Spanish, French, Portuguese, German or Luxembourgish.
• Prior experience in a matrix organisation or in the country or regional unit of a multinational group.

4 Personal attributes

• Commercial and pragmatic. Comfortable taking a risk-based position and defending it to the Board.
• Comfortable operating hands on in a lean team while also delegating and developing others.
• Able to work across cultures and time zones, and to hold credibility with founders, investors, regulators and counterparties.
• Willing to work in a business whose content categories include adult material.

Requisition ID 124840 - Luxembourg - Experienced Professionals

Your team

The Pictet Group is one of the world's leading independent wealth and asset managers. Founded in 1805 and headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland, the Group is represented at 30 offices in financial centres worldwide, and currently employs over 5200 people. Pictet has been present since 1989 in Luxembourg, where it employs over 700 people.
